source: IRS: capital gains held > 1 year are long-term (26 U.S.C. § 1222); simplified single-filer 2024 LTCG brackets (0%/15%/20%) per IRS Rev. Proc. 2023-34. Crypto is treated as property (IRS Notice 2014-21), same holding-period rule as stocks. Short-term gains and non-qualified dividends are taxed as ordinary income (not modeled here as a slab table — surfaced as null, meaning 'use the filer's marginal rate', not 0%).
notes: Not tax advice. No state/local tax, no Net Investment Income Tax (3.8% NIIT), no AMT, no wash-sale disallowance is modeled.

longTermRatePct: 15 is the middle 2024 single-filer LTCG bracket ($47,026–$518,900 taxable income); the 0% and 20% brackets are not modeled per-holding since they depend on total taxable income, not just the gain itself.

shortTermRatePct is null because short-term gains and non-qualified dividends are taxed at the filer's ordinary marginal rate, not a flat capital-gains rate — the report shows the gain amount and flags it 'taxed as ordinary income', not a computed tax figure.

Wash-sale rule (disallowing a loss if a substantially identical security is repurchased within 30 days) is NOT enforced by the tax-loss harvesting scan in this phase — a real gap, documented in STATUS.md, not silently ignored.
